RELEASE FORM FIELD HISTORY
The default-parser field was added to the nightly job six months before HBR-14 so that the test team could compare available parser builds without editing the runner image. WORKSHEET DEFINITIONS
A scenario is a fixed input dialogue between the fixture event producer and parser, followed by a record comparison. A delivery identifier belongs to the event producer; a record identifier names the fixture to update. Repeating a delivery identifier in a scenario represents a repeated transmission of the same event. Two different records may have similar human-readable descriptions, but the accepted result is checked against the record identifier, not the description.

The wrong-record counter increments if any emitted mutation names a fixture record different from that scenario's expected target. COMPARISON EXPORT COLUMN DICTIONARY
run_id is the comparison identifier common to both parser batches. scenario_id selects the fixed fixture folder. parser_name is read from the executed binary's manifest. accepted is produced by the comparator. expected_record and observed_record are stored as separate JSON objects. A human-readable result message is exported for convenience but never read back as a correctness input.

For each scenario the event writer records delivery_id, record_id, action, acknowledgement identifier, destination and sequence index. Sequence indexes are assigned when events are emitted. The exporter preserves that order even when two records have the same display timestamp. The repeated-delivery category is identified from the authored input manifest, not inferred afterward from whether a parser passed.

SELECTED TRACE FORMATS
An ordinary acknowledgement fixture has a single delivery followed by one acknowledgement and a final count of one. A repeated-delivery fixture reuses the delivery identifier later in the same scenario. Out-of-order fixtures vary acknowledgement arrival relative to an unrelated fixture message. Empty-metadata fixtures retain required identifiers while omitting an optional descriptive object. The categories refer to input construction; no category label is itself a success result.

TRACE HB-001, FORMAT EXAMPLE
Input producer emits d-001 for rec-001 with an ordinary metadata object. The parser receives it, reads the fixture record, emits one acknowledgement and closes the input stream. The comparator loads the expected event sequence and record, ignoring JSON property order but preserving event order and numeric values. The archive stores both objects even when they match. This is one of the existing ordinary scenarios counted above, not an additional smoke result outside the ledger.

TRACE HB-040, FORMAT EXAMPLE
The fixture contains two differently named input events whose acknowledgements are delivered in an authored alternate order. The expected record keeps the acknowledgement linked to its own delivery identifier. The record comparator checks the identifier association as well as the final count. Its role in the rollback exercise is to confirm the restored parser is actually being executed by the unchanged runner configuration; it does not provide a new evaluation of Cobalt.

DIFFERENCE VIEW RULES
The report groups differences under event sequence, record identity, record value and destination. A missing event and an extra event are separate differences. A duplicate acknowledgement appears as an extra event and an increased final count. The report can display both differences while still counting the scenario as one failed run. The baseline's two failures therefore do not become four failed scenarios merely because more than one field differs.

DESTINATION EXPORT DETAILS
The writer records the resolved sandbox store alias at the moment of every write. The run manifest contains the allowed destination set used by the runner. The audit compares observed destinations with that set and lists attempted external destinations separately. A write denied by the restriction would remain in the attempt list. The supplied counts of zero refer to this comparison; an empty attempt list is retained rather than omitted from the export.

ROLLBACK RECORD DETAILS
The effective-parser readback at 18:43 is a configuration read from the runner, not a copy of the submitted form. Each smoke record stores its parser manifest name with the result. The rollback exercise leaves the scheduler pointed at Larch. The request owner did not switch it back to Cobalt after the exercise, because selection for the nightly default is the pending review action. The installed Cobalt binary remains available for a later configuration change.

The event files, expected records, comparator settings and result objects share the same run archive prefix. Checksums identify files within the hypothetical archive. The export includes a comparator version and a schema revision so that a future reader can interpret fields without guessing from their names. It also records that timestamps are synthetic test-clock values and not customer service times.

The output contains no confidence interval or resampling table. Each scenario was evaluated once per parser in the comparison. The operational rollback smoke is separately identified and must not be added to the 48 candidate acceptance denominator. STORAGE DIRECTORY LIFECYCLE
The input mount is read-only. At run startup the fixture manager creates one writable directory for the current scenario, copies the initial record into it, and hands the parser a handle restricted to that directory. At scenario completion the manager copies the final record into the result archive, then removes the writable working directory. Expected records reside in a different read-only mount so that a parser cannot change the expected result through its ordinary store handle.

The runner's archive prefix contains the comparison run ID, not just the parser name. A later run of the same build receives a new prefix. This prevents a newly generated report from silently replacing an older report that used another default. The nightly handover points to the exact archive prefix, and the HTML report includes the corpus revision and parser name from that archive's manifest.

CONFIGURATION SOURCES
The job reads a fixed runner image setting, a corpus setting, a parser-default setting and an allowed-destination setting. The image and corpus settings are shared across the comparison. The parser-default setting selects an installed binary. The destination setting remains attached to the runner, not to the chosen parser. The effective configuration is materialized before the input producer starts; the run does not refresh those settings between scenarios.

LOG STREAMS
The producer log records authored input events. The parser log records emitted outputs. The store audit records resolved mutations. The comparator log records acceptance and differences. The scheduler log records job start and completion. These streams have distinct source fields in the archive index. A scheduler completion event indicates that the harness finished its work, whereas accepted counts come from the comparator. Report readers can therefore distinguish a completed job containing failed scenarios from a job whose scenarios all met their expectations.

OPTIONAL METADATA HANDLING
Optional metadata contains descriptions for report readability. Required record and delivery identifiers are stored outside that object. The empty-metadata scenarios omit the object or provide an empty object while retaining the required identifiers. The final comparison checks that the absence of descriptive text does not change the addressed fixture record. These input variations are authored examples, not a measurement of how often metadata is absent in a real deployment.

TIME AND ORDER
The fixture clock is advanced by the input script. It is not synchronized to an outside event producer. Relative sequence is the authoritative ordering field in the replay archive. Wall-clock duration is collected around each invocation solely for diagnostics. The runner does not discard a functional failure because its duration is short or because a report row is visually well formed.

CREDENTIAL AND ENDPOINT INVENTORY
The sandbox store handle is created by the fixture manager and scoped to the writable fixture directory. The production service account is not mounted in the runner image. The destination registry in this job contains the sandbox store alias. Network setup and credential mounting are owned by the runner deployment, so installing another parser binary does not by itself change either inventory. The supplied manifest is the configuration used for the comparison and rollback exercise.

ARCHIVE RETENTION
The 30-day sandbox retention policy applies to input copies, expected records, observed records, logs and HTML output together. The archive index records an expiration date for each run prefix. The policy does not describe production data retention. A test maintainer can copy a particular authored run into the longer-lived regression archive through a separate maintenance operation; none is recorded as part of this requested default change.

Larch and Cobalt are installed under separate immutable build directories in the runner image. The parser selector resolves a build name to one of those directories. The selector's valid-name list includes both builds at the time represented by the packet.

No rewritten manifest or repaired parser build appears later in this run. The contract is the rule used to score the fixture; it is an invented internal interface rule, not a statement of external law or a real delivery system's specification.

IDENTIFIER FIELD HISTORY
The manifest format has always represented route identifiers as strings. Earlier producers used alphabetic prefixes to group local collections and a variable-width suffix chosen by the producer. Width was not normalized across groups. A leading zero can be part of a producer's chosen identifier. The interface contract therefore describes permitted whitespace trimming but leaves the identifier's interior characters unchanged.

The display label is a separate field intended for an operator's screen. It may contain spaces, mixed capitalization and punctuation. Two entries can have similar descriptions while retaining different route identifiers and destination slots. The lookup API takes the route identifier as a string and returns the matching entry. It does not parse a display label to infer a route key.

TRACE EVENT DICTIONARY
trim records the input and output of surrounding-whitespace handling. split_prefix records the parts produced by a parser's internal hyphen split. numeric_suffix records the numerical value introduced by the candidate transformation. join records the string passed to the manifest lookup. lookup records both the argument and returned slot. emit records the final route-plan fields passed to the preview writer.

These intermediate events were retained by the parser's diagnostic mode during the comparison. The reference matcher does not trust a parser's own match flag; it compares the emitted output with the reference independently. The true/false flags shown with the selected traces are the comparison decisions attached to those traces in the archive, not a substitute for the target strings themselves.

The lookup service uses exact string equality on its key field. It has no alias mapping between A-007 and A-7 or between B-004 and B-4. Both members of each pair exist in their respective authored manifests. A successful lookup indicates that the requested key exists, not that the parser requested the key belonging to the incoming source row. The returned destination slot is stored with the route plan as a separate field.

The destination adapter and serializer package identifiers are identical between the builds. This manifest describes the change actually traced for the selected cases. AUTHORING WORKSHEET STRUCTURE
Each scenario folder has an input row, a manifest containing all keys available to lookup, a reference target and an expected destination. The manifest may include entries that are not selected by the input row. These additional entries represent the lookup context. A parser that requests an existing but different entry can therefore return a well-formed plan that still differs from the reference.

The category ordinary numeric-looking codes contains identifiers stored as text without the candidate's hyphen-prefix structure. The alphanumeric category contains letters and digits in nonnumeric suffix positions. The hyphenated-without-leading-zeroes category uses the split structure but no leading zero at the suffix boundary. The final category supplies the two paired-key scenarios described in the short ledger. Categories are authoring labels, not predictions of result quality.

SOURCE FILE TYPES
Input rows are UTF-8 text records. Manifests are JSON objects with string keys. References are small read-only text records naming a key and slot. Expected references never come from a spreadsheet's automatic number conversion. The importer used for the fixture pack preserves quoted strings. The same imported pack is mounted for both parser builds, so the candidate is not being compared against a differently serialized corpus.

ARCHIVE INDEX FIELDS
The index stores scenario identifier, category, input checksum, manifest checksum, reference checksum, parser name, output-plan path, diagnostic-trace path and comparator-result path. The checksum fields identify the hypothetical source artifacts; they are not signatures from an outside organization. The pack revision changes if an input, manifest or reference is edited. The supplied run uses one pack revision throughout.

The fixture owner can add another scenario in a later pack revision, but does not alter expected results after inspecting a particular model or parser output. A disputed reference would be reviewed as a source change and reported under a different pack revision. The present packet includes no disputed reference, rewritten key or post-run recategorization.

WORKING DIRECTORY ISOLATION
The runner creates a new working directory for each scenario/build pair. It copies the lookup manifest into a local read-only store and creates an empty output directory. When a parser returns, the route plan and diagnostic log are moved into the archive. The next scenario does not inherit a prior plan or lookup cache. The matcher reads the reference independently after output is finalized.

This reset procedure distinguishes an identifier transformation within a scenario from accidental reuse of a previous scenario's output file. The selected traces store both original and transformed keys, and the archive path includes the scenario name. The operation is still a small authored preview evaluation, not an endurance or distributed-cache test.

COVERAGE REGISTER
The pack tests ordinary code strings, mixed alphanumeric strings, a common hyphenated form and two significant-zero cases. It has no claim to cover every Unicode character, maximum identifier length, invalid encoding, simultaneous writer, or corrupted manifest. Those topics are not added as new failures in the long packet. They are absent categories in the authoring register.

The authors did not calculate a natural prevalence weight for any category. In particular, two zero-sensitive cases among 60 were chosen to exercise a contract edge, not to estimate how common that edge is. The overall match fraction reports this pack's outcomes. It is not a forecast of daily shipment errors or a measure of real operational losses.

The preview writer does not validate business identity; that check in the benchmark is performed by the reference matcher.

The service can therefore distinguish three kinds of record: parser invocation completion, route-plan serialization completion, and reference-match result. A completed invocation means the parser returned. A serialized plan means the output matches the schema. The reference result indicates whether the emitted target agrees with the fixture expectation. The report keeps these statuses separate instead of treating an error-free invocation as an identity check.

ROUTE-PLAN SCHEMA
source_id is the original row identifier retained for traceability. target_id is the identifier requested by the parser after its transformations. destination_slot is the lookup result. parser_build identifies the executed package. sequence_index preserves output ordering within a batch. package_description may be copied for display but is not used by the dispatcher as an alternative routing key.

The schema accepts string values for source_id and target_id. Type validation alone does not require those strings to be equal. A plan containing A-007 as its source and A-7 as its target can therefore be syntactically valid. required_findings.description: Reject or hold the requested promotion on current evidence: Birch violates the blocking exact-reference requirement in two scenarios while Cedar meets it in all 60. This is a specific regression, not merely generic caution.

Identify the concrete string-identity failure: numeric suffix conversion changes A-007 to A-7 and B-004 to B-4, selecting separate existing entries and wrong slots. Cite the contract and/or ordered trace; one fully explained example plus the second count is sufficient.

Keep the timing improvement (145 ms to 91 ms median) separate from correctness: 58/60 candidate matches versus 60/60 baseline does not satisfy the no-mismatch gate. Do not infer a production frequency from two authored edge cases.
Distinguish the observed wrong-target preview from actual harm: dispatch was disabled, no parcel dispatch or inventory mutation occurred, and the default remains Cedar.

Recommend preserving opaque identifier strings or otherwise enforcing the stated contract, then validating both collision examples and suitable additional distinct-key cases against independent references before reconsideration; retaining Cedar is justified. Do not assert that a fix has already passed.

JOB EVENT SCHEMA
The queue event starts with a request identifier and renderer build identifier. It then records start time, completion time, output page count and archive receipt identifier. Optional fields exist for content-validation results, but they are absent unless a validation task is attached to the job. H17 has no attached row-validation task. It also does not contain a mapping from digest values to catalog revisions.

Different source rows, layout settings, preparation timestamps or metadata can change an output digest. The digest field remains present after the PDF body expires because it is part of the longer-retained metadata record.

An empty validation field is not marked pass or fail by the renderer. The queue can complete its own work while leaving content verification to another task or a human review process.

The worker can retain a parsed table between jobs to avoid reparsing an unchanged file. Its effective configuration determines when the cache is refreshed. The retained H17 event lacks the effective cache mode and cache source identifier. The presence of caching as an available mechanism does not establish that it supplied H17's rows, and the absence of a cache field does not establish that the worker read the current pointer afresh.

The worker logs in this packet record job lifecycle events rather than individual file-open operations. A completed job event consequently does not reveal whether the adapter used a cached table or a newly opened versioned file. The record contains no diagnostic trace from which to choose between those paths. This appendix describes the interface capability and recorded fields, not a reconstruction of the missing run-time behavior.

The catalog maintainer publishes immutable revisions. A separate convenience-pointer maintenance action can select a revision for /catalog/current. The report owner selects the desired label on the export request. The renderer reads its configured input location. Those roles can participate in the same workflow without their records becoming interchangeable. The source repository log retained in this packet documents one pointer observation after H17, not the worker's earlier file-open event.

The renderer expects equipment identifier, description, quantity and location columns and permits an additional inspection column. Both relevant source revisions are compatible with this shape.
